lessonMeta.focus: Basic adverbs of frequency in routine descriptions
lessonMeta.canDo: I can describe how often I do simple study or work actions.
outputTargets: Use basic adverbs of frequency.
Connect frequency to a routine action.
Describe simple recurring habits.

arena.speech:
Mission: now you learn to say how often you do things.

In real work and study life, it is not enough to say what you do. You also need to say how frequently it happens:

I always check my tasks.
I usually study at night.
I sometimes use Slack.
I never miss class.

This is the language of habit and consistency.

options.feedback: Excellent. That is a correct simple present sentence with an adverb of frequency.
Not the best pattern for this course stage. Use the more stable model: I usually study at night.

options.text: I am usually study at night.
options.feedback: Do not add am before the main verb here. Say: I usually study at night.

theory.title: Adverbs of Frequency
theory.intro: This lesson introduces the language of frequency and habit. The learner now adds a new layer to routine language by indicating how often actions happen.
content: Common adverbs of frequency at this level are always, usually, often, sometimes and never.
In simple present routine sentences, these adverbs usually come before the main verb.
Examples: I always check my tasks. I usually study at night.
These words help the learner describe patterns, not just isolated actions.
At this stage, the priority is meaning control and stable sentence position.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I study usually at night. → Better in this course model: I usually study at night.
Incorrect: I am always check my tasks. → Correct: I always check my tasks.
Incorrect: I never misses class. → Correct: I never miss class.

theory_pt.title: Advérbios de Frequência
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição introduz a linguagem de frequência e hábito. O aluno agora adiciona uma nova camada à linguagem de rotina ao indicar com que frequência as ações acontecem.
content: Advérbios de frequência comuns neste nível são always, usually, often, sometimes e never.
Em frases de rotina no simple present, esses advérbios geralmente vêm antes do verbo principal.
Exemplos: I always check my tasks. I usually study at night.
Essas palavras ajudam o aluno a descrever padrões, não apenas ações isoladas.
Nesta fase, a prioridade é o controle de significado e a posição estável na frase.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: I study usually at night. → Melhor neste modelo do curso: I usually study at night.
Incorreto: I am always check my tasks. → Correto: I always check my tasks.
Incorreto: I never misses class. → Correto: I never miss class.

theory.title: Frequency in Tech Routine
theory.intro: This lesson applies adverbs of frequency to digital behavior and platform habits. The learner now describes regular interaction with tools, messages, projects and deadlines.
content: Frequency language becomes more useful when connected to real digital actions.
Use stable patterns such as I often use GitHub or I usually read messages in the morning.
This lesson combines adverbs of frequency, simple present verbs and time expressions.
The goal is to describe real repeated behavior in a modern work or study environment.
The sentence should remain short, correct and reusable.
examples: I usually read messages in the morning.
I sometimes work on my project at night.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I use often GitHub. → Better in this course model: I often use GitHub.

content: A linguagem de frequência se torna mais útil quando conectada a ações digitais reais.
Use padrões estáveis como I often use GitHub ou I usually read messages in the morning.
Esta lição combina advérbios de frequência, verbos no simple present e expressões de tempo.
O objetivo é descrever comportamento repetido real em um ambiente moderno de trabalho ou estudo.

aulas.subtitulo: How Often Do You...? — Asking About Habits

lessonMeta.focus: Questions and answers about frequency and recurring actions
lessonMeta.canDo: I can ask and answer simple questions about how often actions happen.
structures: How often do you check your email?
I usually check my email in the morning.
outputTargets: Ask about frequency.
Answer with adverbs or recurring time expressions.
Sustain a simple habit-based exchange.

arena.speech:
Mission: ask about habits and frequency.

Now you move from statements to questions:

How often do you study?
How often do you check your email?
I study every day.
I usually check my email in the morning.

This is the language of recurring behavior.

options.feedback: Excellent. That is the correct question to ask about frequency.
Not correct here. Use the auxiliary do: How often do you study?
Do not use are here. Use the pattern: How often do you study?

theory.title: Questions About Frequency
theory.intro: This lesson teaches the learner how to ask about recurring actions and habits. It is a crucial bridge toward more autonomous interaction and is strongly aligned with the transition from strong A1 to early A2 behavior.
content: Use How often do you...? to ask about the frequency of an action.
Examples: How often do you study? How often do you check your email?
Answers can use adverbs of frequency or recurring time expressions such as every day and every week.
The question pattern depends on the auxiliary do.
At this stage, the learner should master a small set of predictable question-answer exchanges.
examples: How often do you check your email?
I usually check my email in the morning.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: How often you study? → Correct: How often do you study?
Incorrect: How often are you check your email? → Correct: How often do you check your email?
Incorrect: I every day study. → Better in this model: I study every day.

theory_pt.title: Perguntas Sobre Frequência
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição ensina o aluno a perguntar sobre ações recorrentes e hábitos. É uma ponte crucial para interação mais autônoma e se alinha fortemente à transição de um A1 forte para um A2 inicial.
content: Use How often do you...? para perguntar sobre a frequência de uma ação.
Exemplos: How often do you study? How often do you check your email?
As respostas podem usar advérbios de frequência ou expressões recorrentes de tempo como every day e every week.
O padrão da pergunta depende do auxiliar do.
Nesta fase, o aluno deve dominar um pequeno conjunto de trocas previsíveis de pergunta e resposta.
examples: Com que frequência você verifica seu email?
Eu geralmente verifico meu email de manhã.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: How often you study? → Correto: How often do you study?
Incorreto: How often are you check your email? → Correto: How often do you check your email?
Incorreto: I every day study. → Melhor neste modelo: I study every day.

theory.title: Building a Habit Profile
theory.intro: The final lesson of Week 5 integrates frequency language, routine descriptions and recurring weekly behavior into a short habit profile. This is a strong bridge toward early A2 communicative flexibility.
content: A habit profile connects frequency, action and context.
At this stage, the learner should use short complete sentences that are easy to repeat and adapt.
Useful patterns include I always + verb, I usually + verb, I sometimes + verb and I never + verb.
The final output should sound real, personal and behavior-based.
The goal is to describe repeated patterns, not isolated moments.
examples: I always study in the morning.
I usually check my tasks after class.
I never miss my English lesson.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I study always in the morning. → Better in this course model: I always study in the morning.
Incorrect: I am never miss my English lesson. → Correct: I never miss my English lesson.

theory_pt.title: Construindo um Perfil de Hábitos
theory_pt.intro: A última lição da Semana 5 integra linguagem de frequência, descrições de rotina e comportamento semanal recorrente em um perfil curto de hábitos. Esta é uma ponte forte para uma flexibilidade comunicativa de A2 inicial.
content: Um perfil de hábitos conecta frequência, ação e contexto.
Nesta fase, o aluno deve usar frases curtas e completas que sejam fáceis de repetir e adaptar.
Padrões úteis incluem I always + verbo, I usually + verbo, I sometimes + verbo e I never + verbo.
A produção final deve soar real, pessoal e baseada em comportamento.
O objetivo é descrever padrões repetidos, não momentos isolados.
examples: Eu geralmente verifico minhas tarefas depois da aula.
Eu às vezes trabalho à noite.
Eu nunca falto à minha aula de inglês.

Incorreto: I often uses GitHub. → Correto: I often use GitHub.

arena.speech:
Mission: now you learn to talk about what you like and do not like.

In real study life, preferences matter. They shape motivation and performance:

theory.title: Likes and Dislikes
theory.intro: This lesson introduces basic preference language with the verbs like and do not like. The learner now adds personal evaluation to study and tech-related communication.
content: Use I like... to express positive preference.
Use I don't like... to express negative preference.
This structure is useful for talking about lessons, activities, tools and study formats.
At this stage, the learner should focus on short complete sentences with clear object nouns.
Preference language helps the learner sound more personal and more autonomous.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I am like video lessons. → Correct: I like video lessons.
Incorrect: I like not long texts. → Better in this course model: I don't like long texts.

theory.title: Using Prefer
theory.intro: This lesson introduces a stronger and more selective preference structure. The learner now moves from simple likes to choosing one option as better or more suitable.
content: Use I prefer... to express stronger preference.
You can also compare options with a simple pattern such as I prefer quizzes to long texts.
At this stage, the learner should focus on short, high-frequency comparisons.
Prefer is especially useful in study and productivity contexts.
The structure should remain direct and easy to repeat.

theory_pt.title: Usando Prefer
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição introduz uma estrutura de preferência mais forte e mais seletiva. O aluno agora passa de gostos simples para a escolha de uma opção como melhor ou mais adequada.
content: Use I prefer... para expressar preferência mais forte.
Você também pode comparar opções com um padrão simples como I prefer quizzes to long texts.
Nesta fase, o aluno deve focar em comparações curtas e de alta frequência.
Prefer é especialmente útil em contextos de estudo e produtividade.
A estrutura deve permanecer direta e fácil de repetir.
examples: Eu prefiro quizzes a textos longos.

aulas.subtitulo: How I Learn Best — Learning Style and Study Support

lessonMeta.focus: Simple learning-style language and support preferences
lessonMeta.canDo: I can describe how I learn better and what kind of support helps me.
outputTargets: Describe simple learning style.
Say what helps me learn.
Connect support tools to study success.

arena.speech:
Mission: now describe how you learn best.

Learning is not only about content. It is also about method and support:

I learn better with examples.
I like short explanations.
I prefer practice and feedback.
I study better with notes.

This is the language of learning style.

options.feedback: Excellent. That is a clear and useful sentence about learning style.

options.text: I am learn better with examples.
options.feedback: Do not use am before learn here. Say: I learn better with examples.
You need the support phrase with examples. Say: I learn better with examples.

theory.title: Learning Style Language
theory.intro: This lesson introduces a simple way to describe preferred learning conditions and study support. It helps the learner speak more personally and more strategically about studying.
content: Use I learn better with... to describe what helps your learning.
You can combine this with like and prefer: I like short explanations, I prefer practice and feedback.
This language is useful in self-description, reflection and guided learning environments.
The learner should use a small set of clear support nouns such as examples, notes, feedback and practice.
At this stage, short and personal sentences are more important than abstract explanation.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I am learn better with examples. → Correct: I learn better with examples.
Incorrect: I learn better examples. → Better in this course model: I learn better with examples.
Incorrect: I prefers practice and feedback. → Correct: I prefer practice and feedback.

theory_pt.title: Linguagem de Estilo de Aprendizagem
theory_pt.intro: Esta lição introduz uma forma simples de descrever condições preferidas de aprendizagem e apoio ao estudo. Ela ajuda o aluno a falar de forma mais pessoal e mais estratégica sobre estudar.
content: Use I learn better with... para descrever o que ajuda sua aprendizagem.
Você pode combinar isso com like e prefer: I like short explanations, I prefer practice and feedback.
Essa linguagem é útil em auto descrição, reflexão e ambientes guiados de aprendizagem.
O aluno deve usar um pequeno conjunto de substantivos claros de apoio como examples, notes, feedback e practice.
Nesta fase, frases curtas e pessoais são mais importantes do que explicações abstratas.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: I am learn better with examples. → Correto: I learn better with examples.
Incorreto: I learn better examples. → Melhor neste modelo do curso: I learn better with examples.
Incorreto: I prefers practice and feedback. → Correto: I prefer practice and feedback.

theory.title: Building a Learning Profile
theory.intro: The final lesson of Week 6 integrates positive preference, negative preference, stronger choice and learning-style language into a short personal profile. This is a strong step toward more autonomous self-expression.
content: A learning profile connects likes, preferences, dislikes and support conditions.
At this stage, the learner should use short complete sentences that are easy to personalize and reuse.
Useful patterns include I like..., I don't like..., I prefer... and I learn better with....
The final output should sound personal, clear and realistic.
The goal is to describe a real study identity, not an abstract opinion list.
examples: I study better with notes and feedback.
commonMistakes: Incorrect: I am like video lessons. → Correct: I like video lessons.
Incorrect: I am prefer coding practice. → Correct: I prefer coding practice.
Incorrect: I learn better examples. → Better in this course model: I learn better with examples.

theory_pt.title: Construindo um Perfil de Aprendizagem
theory_pt.intro: A última lição da Semana 6 integra preferência positiva, preferência negativa, escolha mais forte e linguagem de estilo de aprendizagem em um perfil pessoal curto. Este é um passo forte rumo a uma autoexpressão mais autônoma.
content: Um perfil de aprendizagem conecta gostos, preferências, desgostos e condições de apoio.
Nesta fase, o aluno deve usar frases curtas e completas que sejam fáceis de personalizar e reutilizar.
Padrões úteis incluem I like..., I don't like..., I prefer... e I learn better with....
A produção final deve soar pessoal, clara e realista.
O objetivo é descrever uma identidade real de estudo, não uma lista abstrata de opiniões.
examples: Eu não gosto de textos longos.
Eu estudo melhor com anotações e feedback.
commonMistakes: Incorreto: I am like video lessons. → Correto: I like video lessons.
Incorreto: I am prefer coding practice. → Correto: I prefer coding practice.
Incorreto: I learn better examples. → Melhor neste modelo do curso: I learn better with examples.
